Hannah (Customer): Hey team — since ~09:30 UTC our app started getting a ton of errors from Redwood. We see 5xx and lots of timeouts. Affected customers in prod-nyc. Example error is 'upstream error: cache fetch failed' and some 504 gateway timeouts. Request IDs: rq_8f3b, rq_8f4c, rq_8f5d. Can you look? We're blocked on a release.
Sam (Support): Acked — I'm triaging. Can you share a full request example (curl) and the API host/region + org id? Also any recent config changes on your side?
Hannah (Customer): Curl + headers below. No config changes on our side. Org: org_42
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" \
  -H "Redwood-Org: org_42" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-7b","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Sam (Support): Thanks. Escalating to SRE and Eng-Runtime. Marking severity=P2 for now since multiple customers affected. @Priya @Marcus can you take a look at cache/KV dependency health for prod-nyc? We suspect Redis/prefix cache issues.
Priya (SRE): I'm on it. Looking at the cache dashboards now — big spike in redis command retries and a jump in 'prefix-miss' error rates starting 09:28 UTC. Also seeing increased memcached evictions on the /kv-prefix layer. Overlayed this with API 5xx rate and it's correlated.
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — service: cache-prefix (prod-nyc) — degraded — paging on call
Priya (SRE): Checking master replicas and connection counts. Initial signs: one Redis node in the cluster reported OOM and got into COW/eviction thrash, then the client library started returning ECONNRESET / ERR 'CLUSTERDOWN'. Runtime codepath assumes cache GETs succeed; when the cache client errors we bubble 5xx or timeout to API gateway. I can reproduce a failing GET from the runtime with a local helper:
```txt
[09:31:45] redis://10.2.5.13:6379 - ERR OOM command 'GET' failed
[09:31:46] client: prefix-cache-connector - error=CLUSTERDOWN
[09:31:47] runtime: kv_fetch for prefix user:org_42:session_1 - error=ECONNRESET
[09:31:48] api-gateway: downstream 504 for rq_8f3b
```
Priya (SRE): Immediate mitigation options:
- fail open on cache errors (treat as cache miss) for non-critical prefixes (fastest, config flip in runtime)
- scale up Redis nodes / add memory on the affected shard (requires infra change)
- promote a healthy replica to master (risky if not fully synced)
Marcus (Eng-Runtime): I can push a temporary config flip to treat cache connector errors as cache misses for the prefix layer. That will reduce 5xx but might increase token costs/latency. I'll trigger a canary rollout to prod-nyc and watch errors.
Sam (Support): Please document the rollout and ETA. Hannah — if we flip to fail-open you'll likely see more cold starts (slower first requests) but fewer 5xx/timeouts. Are you OK with that tradeoff?
Hannah (Customer): Yes, please do fail-open. Better to have slower responses than errors. Also please share repro steps so we can validate on our side.
Marcus (Eng-Runtime): Pushing canary now. Config: `REDWOOD_CACHE_FAIL_OPEN=true` for service 'runtime-prefix' with 10% canary. Rolling logs:
```txt
[10:05:12] rollout-controller: starting canary for runtime-prefix (prod-nyc) 10%
[10:07:03] runtime-012: cache-error-mode=fail_open
[10:07:05] runtime-013: cache-error-mode=fail_open
[10:12:41] rollout-controller: canary metrics: 5xx rate down 78% on canary nodes
```
Marcus (Eng-Runtime): Canary looks good. Promoting to 100% now. I'll post when complete.
Priya (SRE): While Marcus is rolling, I'm starting a controlled scale-up of the Redis shard and preparing to failover the OOM node if it doesn't recover. Also bumping eviction thresholds and inspecting key TTL patterns — looks like a churny prefix pattern from a background job in one customer workspace causing cache bloat.
Marcus (Eng-Runtime): 100% rollout complete at 10:25 UTC. Observed error rate dropped to baseline. API 5xx and 504s are dropping. Leaving tracing on for another hour.
Sam (Support): Hannah — can you confirm your requests are succeeding now? Any 5xx in the last 10 minutes?
Hannah (Customer): Confirmed — we see successful responses now. Latency is a bit higher on a few calls but acceptable. Thanks. We'll also audit our background job for cache key churn (we found a cron that rehashed user sessions every 20s — fixing it now).
Priya (SRE): Next steps (tracked in our internal ticket):
- investigate root cause of cache bloat and customer job patterns (follow-up with tenant team)
- bring affected Redis node back with larger memory and run full resync
- add stronger circuit-breaker for prefix-cache client in runtime to fail fast to fallback path
- add alert thresholds for 'prefix-miss' churn and memcached eviction delta
Sam (Support): Closing loop: severity downgraded. I'll update the customer-facing incident note and leave the support ticket open until Redis resync completes. Thanks @Priya @Marcus for fast action. :thumbsup:
Hannah (Customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please ping when Redis is fully healthy and the root-cause ticket is created so we can reference it internally.
Marcus (Eng-Runtime): Noted — creating an RFC for safer default: fail-open on prefix cache + better telemetry. Will link the PR and follow-ups in the incident ticket.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — cache-prefix (prod-nyc) — mitigated — monitor
Sam (Support): Thread summary for records: cause = Redis OOM + eviction thrash on prefix KV layer -> client errors -> runtime bubbled 5xx/504s. Mitigation = fail-open config flip + Redis scale-up in progress. Customer validated success. Ticket: INC-2026
